heading: REGENT OF SOUTHEAST MINAHASA PROVINCE OF NORTH SULAWESI
translated_text:
REGENT OF SOUTHEAST MINAHASA PROVINCE OF NORTH SULAWESI

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTHEAST MINAHASA REGENCY NUMBER 8 OF 2016

heading: CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
translated_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Southeast Minahasa Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the Principles of Autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible Autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Southeast Minahasa.
5. Provincial Government is the Provincial Government of North Sulawesi.
6. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Institution of Southeast Minahasa Regency as an element of Regional Government administration.
7. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is a Regional Government Work Unit related to the implementation of child protection.
8. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional financial plan that is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and DPRD and stipulated by Regional Regulation.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
10. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
11. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
12. Special protection is a form of protection received by a Child in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
16. Community is families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Social Organization hereinafter referred to as Orsos is an institution/foundation/social association formed by the community whether legally incorporated or not legally incorporated which functions as a means of community participation in implementing Social Welfare Efforts (UKS).
18. Child Protection Social House hereinafter abbreviated as RSPA is a child protection service unit for child victims of violence and child trafficking as a continuation of temporary shelter which functions to provide protection, recovery, rehabilitation, advocacy and referral.
19. Social Services for Children are physical, mental and social services aimed at helping children to grow and develop properly.
20. Social Services for Neglected Children are social services for children whose parents do not have the ability to meet the needs of children to grow and develop properly.
21. Child-friendly school is an educational institution that recognizes and respects children's rights to obtain education, health, opportunities to play and have fun, protection from violence and abuse, can express views freely, and participate in making decisions according to their capacity.
22. Social Work Profession is a profession based on a framework of science, values and technical skills and can be used as a vehicle in the implementation of social welfare efforts.
23. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons as well as women and children victims of violence.
24. Violence Victim Protection Forum hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of women and child victims of violence whose implementation is networked and formed at the Regency, District and Village levels.

heading: Article 2
Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

The objectives of Victim Protection are:

a. to prevent violence against women and children;
b. to provide services to Victims; and
c. to empower women victims of violence.

heading: Article 4
translated_text:
Article 4

The scope of protection for victims includes prevention, service, empowerment and handling efforts for victims of violence in the Region.

heading: CHAPTER II VIOLENCE
Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that which results in pain, illness or serious injury.

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c includes:

a. forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the scope of that household and/or outside the scope of that household; and
b. forced sexual intercourse against a person within the scope of their household with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

Domestic neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is:

a. the act of neglecting a person within the scope of the household whereas according to the law applicable to the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care or maintenance to that person.
b. the act of neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to him/her or because of an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; and
c. an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is caused by:

a. an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all prostitution or indecency activities.

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

Other violence as referred to in Article 5 letter f is caused by:

a. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether or not using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

heading: CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
Article 13
CHAPTER IV OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

The Regional Government provides services for victims of violence in the form of:

a. facilitating the establishment of PPT;
b. facilitating PPT facilities and infrastructure according to regional financial capacity; and
c. facilitating FPKK as a network forum for handling victims of violence.

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to:

a. supervise the implementation of services for victims of violence, with minimum service standards; and
b. provide funds for victim protection through the APBD and/or other lawful regional financial sources.

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

In implementing the obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in Article 14, Article 15 and Article 16, the Regent grants authority to the agency that has the main tasks and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Article 19
CHAPTER V VICTIM PROTECTION
translated_text:
CHAPTER V VICTIM PROTECTION

Article 20

1. Efforts to prevent violence against women and children are carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the agency that has the main tasks and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
2. Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by:

a. forming a work network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
c. establishing a violence prevention system; and
d. conducting socialization about laws and regulations related to the protection of women and child victims of violence.

heading: Article 21
CHAPTER VI INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER

Article 22

1. PPT is established by the Regional Government in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit (UPT).
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is a functional work unit that has the task, principal, and function of providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
3. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is tasked with providing services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house for victims of violence.
4. In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (3), then victims of violence are referred to PPT that has a safe house.
5. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. The organizational structure of PPT established by the Regional Government as referred to in Article 22 paragraph (1) consists of:

a. General Chairperson:
b. Secretary:
c. Treasurer; and
d. Executive Chairperson who oversees fields.

2. The fields as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, at a minimum include:

a. complaint service field:
b. health service field:
c. social rehabilitation service field;
d. repatriation and social reintegration field; and
e. legal aid service field.

3. In carrying out duties, PPT is responsible to the Regent through the Head of the agency that has the main tasks and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Article 24
Article 25
Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

The social rehabilitation service field as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter c has the task of:

a. providing assistance during the case handling process; and
b. conducting counseling.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

The repatriation and social reintegration field as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter d has the task of:

a. conducting coordination with relevant agencies for victim repatriation;
b. making progress reports on the repatriation assistance process and social rehabilitation; and
c. conducting monitoring for at least three months after the victim is returned to their family.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

The legal aid service field as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter e has the task of:

a. accompanying and defending every legal service process; and
b. making progress reports on legal handling.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

1. PPT established by the Regional Government has at least three counselors.
2. Counselors as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. counselor in the field of law;
b. counselor in the field of health; and
c. counselor in the field of psychology.

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

Further provisions regarding the development, mechanism and networked working relationship of PPT shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Part One
translated_text:
Part One

Services

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

1. The provision of services to victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner by PPT.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.

heading: Article 32
Article 33
Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

Complaint, consultation, and counseling services as referred to in Article 33 letter a include:
a. initial identification or recording of victims; and
b. informed consent.

heading: Article 35
Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

Health services as referred to in Article 33 letter c include:
a. first aid to victims;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and
c. referral to health services.

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 33 letter d constitute services provided by assistants in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and provide social support so that victims have self-confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems, by:
a. providing spiritual guidance to victims; and
b. psychological recovery of victims.

heading: Article 38
Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

1. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 33 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
2. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. Regency/City Governments within one Provincial area; and
b. related government and non-government agencies and institutions.

heading: Part Two Empowerment
translated_text:
Part Two Empowerment

Paragraph 1 Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

Article 40

Forms of empowerment of women victims of violence include:
a. job training;
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups; and
c. capital assistance.

heading: Article 41
heading_path: Paragraph 1 Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence
translated_text:
Article 41

Job training as referred to in Article 40 letter a includes:
a. skills training;
b. field work practice; and
c. apprenticeship.

heading: Article 42
heading_path: Paragraph 1 Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence
translated_text:
Article 42

Productive economic enterprises and joint business groups as referred to in Article 40 letter b include:
a. entrepreneurial skills training;
b. facilitation of joint business group formation; and
c. business implementation assistance.

heading: Article 43
heading_path: Paragraph 1 Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence
translated_text:
Article 43

Capital assistance as referred to in Article 40 letter c includes:
a. work facilities and infrastructure assistance; and
b. facilitation of working capital assistance.

heading: Paragraph 2 Fulfillment of the Rights of Child Victims of Violence
translated_text:
Paragraph 2 Fulfillment of the Rights of Child Victims of Violence

Article 44

1. The Regional Government, PPT, and the community are obliged to fulfill the rights of child victims of violence.
2. Forms of fulfillment of the rights of child victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include the fulfillment of children's basic rights according to their needs.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Coordination of Victim Protection

heading: Article 45
translated_text:
Article 45

1. In an effort to provide and organize service delivery for victims, the Regional Government shall establish FPKK.
2. FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to:
a. coordinate and synchronize PPT service delivery;
b. maintain and develop networks and referral systems; and
c. collect, compile and present reports on violence.
3. The management and membership of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.
4. The membership of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be grouped into the following roles:
a. health role;
b. psychology role;
c. legal role;
d. social role; and
e. economic role.
5. Further provisions regarding the establishment, main duties, and functions as well as membership of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 46

1. The Regional Government shall conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of minimum service standards for every PPT in the Region.
2. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.
4. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, funding, quality, control and supervision.
5. Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted in accordance with laws and regulations.
6. Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted periodically every 6 months.

heading: CHAPTER VIII FUNDING
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII FUNDING

Article 47

Funding for victim protection activities carried out by the Regional Government shall be borne by the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD) and/or other lawful and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER IX COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
CHAPTER X SANCTIONS
translated_text:
CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 49

1. Every person who commits any form of violence as referred to in Article 5 shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
2. For SKPD that do not implement the provisions of Article 14, Article 15 and Article 16, administrative sanctions shall be imposed.
3. Every person who directly witnesses violence as referred to in Article 5 and does not report it to the competent authorities shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

heading: I. GENERAL
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection measures at the Regional level, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

heading: Article 2
translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of victims' basic rights.

Letter b What is meant by "justice" is a state where every person, both men and women, is treated equally and obtains equal opportunities to gain access and welfare;

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter e What is meant by "empowerment" is the strengthening of victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

Article 12

Letter a What is meant by "the right to have one's dignity and honor as a human being respected" is upholding human rights.

Letter b Sufficiently clear.

Letter c Sufficiently clear.

Letter d What is meant by "the right to obtain information" is the right to obtain statements, declarations, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read that are presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology either electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.

Letter e Sufficiently clear.

Letter f What is meant by "the right to compensation" includes: economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health insurance, and education or skills training.

Letter g What is meant by "the right to social rehabilitation" includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, and citizenship.

Letter h What is meant by "the right to complaint handling" is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.

Letter i Sufficiently clear.

Letter j What is meant by "the right to assistance" includes among others: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious counselors, advocates, and family members.

Letter d Sufficiently clear.

Letter e What is meant by "the right to obtain freedom" is the freedom to express one's views on all matters, including those related to legal processes, care and temporary protection as well as identification and implementation of subsequent solutions.

Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by "network" includes: family partners, dasawisma, family groups existing in the Region.

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

Letter a Prevention efforts within the family and/or closest relatives can be conducted by strengthening resilience within the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication among family members.

Letter b Prevention efforts within the community include: fostering environmental awareness of acts of violence occurring in their environment.

Letter c Educational institutions can participate in efforts to provide educational punishment, endeavor to eliminate provisions that do not favor victims of violence.

Letter d What is meant by "community institutions" are institutions formed by members of the community of Citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.

For PPT that do not have a shelter, they can network with PPT that have a shelter.

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2) What is meant by "other service units" is a unified unit that carries out integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence. This service unit can be located at the Integrated Service Center (PPT) and Integrated Crisis Center (PKT) based in Hospitals, Community Health Centers, Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment (P2TP2A), Women and Children Service Unit (UPPA), Trauma Center Shelter (RPTC), Child Social Shelter (RPSA), BP4, and other sub-district-level institutions, prosecutor's offices, courts, Women Crisis Center (WCC), and other similar institutions. This service can be in the form of one roof (one stop crisis center) or in the form of a network, depending on the needs in each region.

heading: Article 35

Article 35

Letter b What is meant by "medico-legal" is medical services to provide optimal professional assistance in utilizing medical science for the purposes of law enforcement and justice. Medico-legal services include, among others: visum et repertum and visum et psikiatrikum.

What is meant by "visum et repertum" is a written statement made by a doctor in forensic medical science at the request of the authorized investigator regarding the results of medical examination of the victim based on their scientific knowledge and under oath, for the purposes of judicial proceedings.

What is meant by "visum et psikiatrikum" is a statement given by a Psychiatrist regarding the mental health condition of the victim required to clarify a case and for the purposes of judicial proceedings.
